newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila eyes stricter rules on backdoor listings.
newsitem.headline: Manila eyes stricter rules on backdoor listings.

text.p: The Philippines' Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is planning to regulate "backdoor listing" and had proposed guidelines for companies, an official document released on Thursday showed.

In a memorandum, the SEC's money market operations department director Linda Daoang said buyers of a substantial stake in a listed company should make a public tender offer to other minority shareholders equal to the price offered to the controlling shareholders.
"Backdoor listing" refers to firms taking over listed firms, mostly dormant companies, and gaining access to the stock market without going through the cumbersome procedures for a new listing.

"A tender offer usually involves widespread solicitation of public shareholders for a substantial percentage of the company's stock ... The price of the tender offer shall be equal to that offered to controlling shareholders," she said.
The buyer should announce the tender offer in a major newspaper within 10 days after it has closed the deal with the majority owners.
"The provisions of the proposed rules are essential to ensuring equal access to the tender offer and fair treatment of all shareholders who wish to tender their shares," Daoang said.
"These rules (are) aimed to provide important new protection for shareholders of registered companies," she added.
The SEC is yet to approve the proposed guidelines.
